source_evidence.observation: The paper defines u as working precision, uf as factorization precision, ur as residual-computation precision, and assumes ur <= u <= uf.
The effective correction-solve precision satisfies u <= us <= uf. Algorithm 1.1 computes an initial solution at uf, residuals at ur rounded to us, corrections at us stored at u, and updates at u.
The analysis invokes the standard floating-point model, defines gamma_k = ku/(1-ku) and gamma_k^r = k ur/(1-k ur), and defines kappa_infinity(A) = ||A^{-1}||_infinity ||A||_infinity.

The step-4 solver contract is ||rhat_i-A dhat_i||_infinity <= us(c1||A||_infinity||dhat_i||_infinity+c2||rhat_i||_infinity). The paper says c1 and c2 are nonnegative functions of n, A, rhat_i, and us.
For an approximate solution y, normwise backward error is defined as the least relative normwise perturbation of A and b, equivalently ||b-Ay||/(||A||||y||+||b||).

The computed residual satisfies rhat_i=b-A xhat_i+Delta r_i with |Delta r_i| <= us|b-A xhat_i|+(1+us)gamma_p^r(|b|+|A||xhat_i|). Here p is the maximum number of nonzeros in a row of [A b], and p=n+1 in the dense case.
The computed update satisfies xhat_{i+1}=xhat_i+dhat_i+Delta x_i with |Delta x_i| <= u|xhat_{i+1}|.
The exact one-step identity is A xhat_{i+1}-b=Delta r_i+A dhat_i-rhat_i+A Delta x_i. The correction defect is h_i=rhat_i-A dhat_i.
Assuming c1 kappa_infinity(A) us < 1, the derivation obtains ||h_i||_infinity <= us(c1 kappa_infinity(A)+c2)/(1-c1 kappa_infinity(A)us) ||rhat_i||_infinity.
For every i >= 0, Theorem 4.1 gives an exact infinity-norm residual recurrence with explicitly defined coefficients alpha_i and beta_i.
The paper separately flags scaling to avoid underflow and overflow when half precision is used; Theorem 4.1 itself does not state an exceptional-value model.

binders: Fix a real linear system Ax=b with A in R^{n x n} and b in R^n; A and b are the working-precision data to which Algorithm 1.1 is applied. [PDF p. 2 (A818), Algorithm 1.1]
Fix unit roundoffs ur, u, us, and uf with ur <= u <= uf and u <= us <= uf; equivalently the combined ordering is ur <= u <= us <= uf. [PDF p. 1 (A817), equation (1.1); PDF p. 2 (A818), us bullet]
Let xhat_i, rhat_i, and dhat_i be the computed iterate, residual, and correction generated by Algorithm 1.1. [PDF p. 2 (A818), Algorithm 1.1; PDF p. 7 (A823), equations (3.3) and (3.6)]
For the fixed system and solver, quantify over every iteration index i >= 0 after imposing the solver and conditioning hypotheses. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
The nonnegative solver quantities c1 and c2 may depend on n, A, rhat_i, and us even though their notation carries no i subscript. [PDF p. 5 (A821), paragraph following equations (2.3)-(2.5)]
hypotheses: Explicit in Theorem 4.1: A is nonsingular. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
Explicit in Theorem 4.1: c1 kappa_infinity(A) us < 1. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]

Explicit in Theorem 4.1: the solver used in step 4 satisfies equation (2.4), namely ||rhat_i-A dhat_i||_infinity <= us(c1||A||_infinity||dhat_i||_infinity+c2||rhat_i||_infinity). [PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.4); PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]

Inherited from the surrounding analysis: residual formation obeys equation (3.3) and the update obeys equation (3.6) under the standard floating-point model. [PDF p. 5 (A821), section 2 opening; PDF p. 7 (A823), equations (3.3) and (3.6)]

Theorem 4.1 requires only solver condition (2.4), not the separate forward-error condition (2.3) or componentwise condition (2.5). [PDF p. 5 (A821), equations (2.3)-(2.5); PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
conclusions: With h_i=rhat_i-A dhat_i, the enclosing derivation proves ||h_i||_infinity <= us[(c1 kappa_infinity(A)+c2)/(1-c1 kappa_infinity(A)us)]||rhat_i||_infinity. [PDF p. 8 (A824), definition of h_i; PDF p. 9 (A825), isolated correction-defect bound]
The exact one-step identity used is A xhat_{i+1}-b=Delta r_i+A dhat_i-rhat_i+A Delta x_i. [PDF p. 8 (A824), equation (4.1)]
For every i >= 0, ||b-A xhat_{i+1}||_infinity <= alpha_i||b-A xhat_i||_infinity+beta_i. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
alpha_i = us[1+(1+us)(c1 kappa_infinity(A)+c2)/(1-c1 kappa_infinity(A)us)]. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1 definition of alpha_i]

beta_i = [1+us(c1 kappa_infinity(A)+c2)/(1-c1 kappa_infinity(A)us)](1+us)gamma_p^r(||b||_infinity+||A||_infinity||xhat_i||_infinity)+u||A||_infinity||xhat_{i+1}||_infinity. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1 definition of beta_i]
definitions_and_conventions: gamma_k=ku/(1-ku), and a superscript r replaces u by ur; hence gamma_p^r=p ur/(1-p ur). [PDF p. 5 (A821), section 2 opening]
p is the maximum number of nonzeros in any row of the augmented matrix [A b]; p=n+1 when A and b are dense. [PDF p. 7 (A823), paragraph preceding equation (3.3)]
Absolute values of vectors and matrices are componentwise, and inequalities between vectors or matrices are interpreted componentwise. [PDF p. 5 (A821), paragraph following equation (2.2)]

Hatted quantities are computed quantities: rhat_i is the computed and rounded residual, dhat_i is the computed correction, and xhat_i is the computed iterate; b-A xhat_i is the exact residual of that computed iterate with respect to the stored data A and b. [PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.4); PDF p. 7 (A823), equations (3.3) and (3.6)]
h_i denotes the correction-equation defect rhat_i-A dhat_i, not a forward error in dhat_i. [PDF p. 8 (A824), text following equation (4.1)]
implicit_context: Theorem 4.1 is embedded in the normwise backward-error analysis, but its literal conclusion is a recurrence for the unnormalized residual norm. [PDF p. 8 (A824), section 4 heading; PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]

The initial solve may use a different solver from the correction solve; no accuracy hypothesis on the step-1 solver or xhat_0 appears in Theorem 4.1. [PDF p. 2 (A818), text following Algorithm 1.1; PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]

The factorization precision uf does not occur in alpha_i or beta_i; its role is inherited only through Algorithm 1.1 and any solver implementation. [PDF p. 2 (A818), Algorithm 1.1 and following text; PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]

The correction-defect estimate is derived from (2.4) using A^{-1} and the identity A dhat_i=rhat_i-h_i; it is not an additional independent hypothesis. [PDF p. 8 (A824), correction-defect derivation; PDF p. 9 (A825), isolated defect bound]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The contract is specifically for Algorithm 1.1: solve initially at uf and store at u; for i=0,1,... compute b-A xhat_i at ur and round it to us; solve the correction equation effectively at us and store the correction at u; then form the update at u. Theorem 4.1 constrains only the step-4 solver through (2.4). [PDF p. 2 (A818), Algorithm 1.1; PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.4); PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
numerical_model: The paper invokes the standard floating-point arithmetic model rather than an exact-real implementation model. [PDF p. 5 (A821), section 2 opening]
Residual formation is two-stage: shat_i=fl_r(b-A xhat_i) is formed at ur, then rhat_i=fl_s(shat_i) is rounded to us. [PDF p. 7 (A823), residual-computation paragraph before equation (3.3)]
The resulting residual perturbation is |Delta r_i| <= us|b-A xhat_i|+(1+us)gamma_p^r(|b|+|A||xhat_i|). [PDF p. 7 (A823), equation (3.3)]

The correction solver is represented by its normwise backward-error contract (2.4), with no requirement in Theorem 4.1 that it be LU, GMRES, or another named solver. [PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.4); PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
The update model is xhat_{i+1}=xhat_i+dhat_i+Delta x_i with |Delta x_i| <= u|xhat_{i+1}|; the error is bounded relative to the computed updated iterate. [PDF p. 7 (A823), equation (3.6)]
error_notions: The theorem controls the norm of the exact residual b-A xhat_i associated with a computed iterate. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]

The solver defect h_i=rhat_i-A dhat_i is the residual of the computed correction equation and is controlled by the normwise solver contract. [PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.4); PDF p. 8 (A824), definition of h_i]

The paper defines normwise backward error eta(y) by relative perturbations to both A and b, equivalently eta(y)=||b-Ay||/(||A||||y||+||b||). Theorem 4.1 does not itself state a bound on this normalized ratio. [PDF p. 5 (A821), definition of eta; PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
No forward-error bound ||x-xhat_i|| occurs in Theorem 4.1. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
norms: Every norm displayed in the defect estimate, residual recurrence, alpha_i, and beta_i is the infinity norm. [PDF p. 9 (A825), isolated defect bound and Theorem 4.1]
The matrix condition number is the infinity-norm condition number ||A^{-1}||_infinity||A||_infinity. [PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.1)]

Componentwise absolute values occur only in the inherited rounding models before norms are taken; they are not a replacement for the theorem's infinity norms. [PDF p. 5 (A821), componentwise convention; PDF p. 7 (A823), equations (3.3) and (3.6); PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
constants_and_indexing: The recurrence holds for i >= 0 and relates iteration i+1 to iteration i. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
The residual-rounding contribution in beta_i uses xhat_i, while the update-rounding contribution uses xhat_{i+1}; this index offset is explicit. [PDF p. 9 (A825), definition of beta_i]
The factors (1+us) occur both inside alpha_i and multiplying gamma_p^r in beta_i. [PDF p. 9 (A825), definitions of alpha_i and beta_i]
The denominator is exactly 1-c1 kappa_infinity(A)us, and the numerator paired with it is c1 kappa_infinity(A)+c2. [PDF p. 9 (A825), defect bound and Theorem 4.1]
gamma_p^r uses p from the augmented sparsity pattern [A b], not merely the row sparsity of A. [PDF p. 7 (A823), paragraph preceding equation (3.3)]
higher_order_terms: Theorem 4.1 retains the rational denominator 1-c1 kappa_infinity(A)us and all displayed products involving (1+us); these are not discarded as higher-order terms. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
gamma_p^r is the rational quantity p ur/(1-p ur), not the first-order replacement p ur. [PDF p. 5 (A821), gamma definition; PDF p. 7 (A823), equation (3.3)]

The theorem uses ordinary <= inequalities and contains no big-O, approximately, or less-than-up-to-constants term. Such approximations first appear in the subsequent Corollary 4.2, not in Theorem 4.1. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.2]
exceptional_values: A must be nonsingular, so A^{-1} and kappa_infinity(A) are defined. [PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.1); PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
The strict condition c1 kappa_infinity(A)us < 1 makes the correction-defect denominator positive. [PDF p. 9 (A825), line before the isolated defect bound and Theorem 4.1]

The cited theorem does not state behavior for NaNs, infinities, overflow, or underflow. The paper only invokes the standard model and separately notes that scaling is important to avoid underflow and overflow in half precision. [PDF p. 5 (A821), section 2 opening; PDF p. 6 (A822), paragraph following Table 2.1]

No hypothesis b != 0 is stated in Theorem 4.1; the residual recurrence itself remains the literal claim even when a normalized backward-error denominator would require separate interpretation. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 5 (A821), definition of eta]

undebatable_constraints: The subject is the computed sequence from Algorithm 1.1, not arbitrary vectors satisfying a recurrence. [PDF p. 2 (A818), Algorithm 1.1; PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
A is a real nonsingular n by n matrix, and the conclusion is universally quantified over i >= 0 after fixing the system and solver. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
The step-4 solver must satisfy the exact two-term normwise condition (2.4), including both c1||A||||dhat_i|| and c2||rhat_i||. [PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.4)]
The condition c1 kappa_infinity(A)us < 1 cannot be weakened or omitted without changing the source claim. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
The conclusion must include the residual recurrence and both complete coefficient formulas alpha_i and beta_i. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
All theorem norms are infinity norms, and kappa_infinity(A) is ||A^{-1}||_infinity||A||_infinity. [PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.1); PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
The beta_i formula must retain gamma_p^r, the factor (1+us), xhat_i in the residual term, and xhat_{i+1} in the update term. [PDF p. 9 (A825), definition of beta_i]
The exact rational coefficients and higher-order factors must not be replaced by first-order or big-O approximations. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]

Theorem 4.1 bounds an unnormalized residual; a backward-stability or limiting-accuracy conclusion belongs to the subsequent corollary and is not part of this theorem. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.2]

ambiguities.issue: c1 and c2 have no displayed iteration subscripts, although the preliminaries say they are functions of rhat_i. [PDF p. 5 (A821), paragraph following equations (2.3)-(2.5)]
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 4.1 writes c1 and c2 inside alpha_i and beta_i without clarifying whether one fixed pair works for every iteration or whether their dependence on i is suppressed. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must either bind iteration-dependent c1 and c2 or explicitly assume uniform constants; silently choosing one interpretation adds information not resolved by the displayed theorem. [PDF p. 5 (A821), solver-assumption paragraph; PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]

ambiguities.issue: The standard floating-point model is cited rather than fully restated in the paper passage. [PDF p. 5 (A821), section 2 opening]
ambiguities.evidence: The definition gamma_p^r=p ur/(1-p ur) is explicit, but the cited pages do not separately state p ur < 1 or enumerate rounding-mode and exceptional-value exclusions. [PDF p. 5 (A821), gamma definition; PDF p. 7 (A823), equation (3.3)]
ambiguities.impact: Those domain and exceptional-value conditions should be labeled inherited or tacit, not presented as explicit hypotheses of Theorem 4.1. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]

ambiguities.issue: us is described as an effective solve-accuracy parameter, not necessarily a distinct hardware format. [PDF p. 2 (A818), us bullet and following paragraph]
ambiguities.evidence: The paper says us describes how accurately the correction equation is solved and takes uf or u in the cases of interest. [PDF p. 2 (A818), paragraph preceding Algorithm 1.1]
ambiguities.impact: The source does not justify restricting Theorem 4.1 to a particular named arithmetic or solver implementation. [PDF p. 2 (A818), Algorithm 1.1; PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]

ambiguities.issue: Algorithm 1.1 says the correction is solved at us and stored at u, but the analysis introduces no separate storage-rounding variable for dhat_i. [PDF p. 2 (A818), Algorithm 1.1 step 4; PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.4)]
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (2.4) directly treats dhat_i as the computed correction supplied to the update, and equation (3.6) adds only the update error Delta x_i. [PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.4); PDF p. 7 (A823), equation (3.6)]
ambiguities.impact: The faithful reading is that any solve-and-storage effects relevant to dhat_i are absorbed into the solver contract; inventing an additional correction-rounding term would alter the displayed result. [PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.4); PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1]

contract_plain_english: Apply the paper's indexed Algorithm 1.1 to a real nonsingular system, using the stated working, residual, effective solve, and factorization precisions. [PDF pp. 1-2 (A817-A818), equation (1.1) and Algorithm 1.1] Assume only that the correction solver obeys the two-term infinity-norm backward-error condition (2.4) and that c1 kappa_infinity(A)us is strictly below one. [PDF p. 5 (A821), equation (2.4); PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1] Then at every iteration the exact residual norm of the next computed iterate is bounded by alpha_i times the current exact residual norm plus beta_i, with alpha_i and beta_i exactly as displayed, including their denominators, (1+us) factors, gamma_p^r term, and the xhat_i versus xhat_{i+1} index placement. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1] The surrounding derivation also gives the exact identity (4.1) and the isolated correction-defect bound. [PDF p. 8 (A824), equation (4.1); PDF p. 9 (A825), isolated defect bound] This theorem is an exact one-step infinity-norm residual recurrence, not by itself an approximate convergence-rate, limiting-residual, forward-error, or normalized backward-stability theorem. [PDF p. 9 (A825), Theorem 4.1 and subsequent Corollary 4.2]
